questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Position Function of an Object Moving With Circular Motion
questions.problem: A particle moves along a **clockwise** circular path with center $O$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity of $3\text{ rad/s}.$ Given that the object is at the position $(2,0)$ when $t=0,$ find the position function of the particle.
questions.worked_solution:
The position function of a particle moving in a circular path of radius $R$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity $\omega $ is given by

$$
r(t)=R(\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t\,j),
$$

where it is assumed that the circle is centered at $O,$ and particle is at the position $(R,0)$ when $t=0.$

Since the object's initial position is $(2,0),$ we have that $r(0)=\,2i,$ and we can conclude that the radius of the circle $R=2.$

Therefore, since we have $R=2$ and $\omega =-3\text{ rad/s}$ (negative because the motion is clockwise), we get that the position function is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =2(\operatorname{cos}⁡(-3t)\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡(-3t)\,j) \\  & =2(\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\,i-\operatorname{sin}⁡3t\,j).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Velocity and Speed of a Particle Moving With Circular Motion
questions.problem: An object moves along a circular path with position $r(t)=4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ meters. Find the speed of the object at time $t,$ measured in seconds.
questions.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

First, we find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(r(t))^{′} \\  & =(4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j)^{′} \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the speed, we calculate the magnitude of the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}||v(t)|| & =\sqrt{(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(4\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16{sin}^{2}⁡t+16{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{16({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the speed of the object is $4\text{ m/s}.$

Note that the speed is constant, but the velocity is not. 

**Method 2**

For uniform circular motion in the $xy$-plane, we have

$$
||v||=R|\omega |,
$$

where $R$ is the radius of the circle, and $\omega $ is the angular velocity.

In our case, the radius of the circle is $R=4\,\text{m}$ and the angular frequency $\omega =1\,\text{rad/s}.$ Therefore,

$$
||v||=4\cdot |1|=4\text{ m/s}.
$$

In our case, we have $R=3$ and $\omega =8\text{ rad/s},$ so we get that the position function is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =3(\operatorname{cos}⁡8t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡8t\,j).\end{aligned}
$$

We find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(3(\operatorname{cos}⁡8t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡8t\,j))^{′} \\  & =-24\operatorname{sin}⁡8t\,i+24\operatorname{cos}⁡8t\,j.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\frac{\pi }{8}) & =-24\operatorname{sin}⁡(8\cdot \frac{\pi }{8})\,i+24\operatorname{cos}⁡(8\cdot \frac{\pi }{8})\,j \\  & =-24\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi \,i+24\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi \,j \\  & =-24\,j\end{aligned}

$$

We find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(7(\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,j))^{′} \\  & =-14\operatorname{sin}⁡2t\,i+14\operatorname{cos}⁡2t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

questions.problem: A particle $P$ moves along a counterclockwise circular path centered at $O$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity of $4\,\text{rad/s}.$ Given that the particle is located at $(5,0)$ when $t=0,$ find the acceleration of the particle at $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$ seconds.
questions.worked_solution:
The position function of a particle moving in a circular path of radius $a$ in the $xy$-plane with a constant angular velocity $\omega $ is given by

$$
r(t)=a(\operatorname{cos}⁡\omega t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡\omega t\,j),
$$

where it is assumed that the circle is centered at $O,$ and the particle is at the position $(a,0)$ when $t=0.$

In our case, we have $a=5$ and $\omega =4\text{ rad/s},$ so we get that the position function is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =5(\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,j).\end{aligned}
$$

We find the velocity and acceleration vectors by differentiating. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(5(\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,j))^{′} \\  & =-20\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,i+20\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,j \\ a(t) & =(-20\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,i+20\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,j)^{′} \\  & =-80\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,i-80\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we find the acceleration vector at $t=\frac{\pi }{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-80\operatorname{cos}⁡(4\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})\,i-80\operatorname{sin}⁡(4\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})\,j \\  & =-80\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\pi )\,i-80\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\pi )\,j \\  & =-80\,i\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: An object moves along a circular path with position $r(t)=\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,j$ meters. Find the magnitude of the acceleration of the object at time $t,$ measured in seconds.
questions.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

First, we find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(r(t))^{′} \\  & =(\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,j)^{′} \\  & =-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we find the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector. 

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =(v(t))^{′} \\  & =(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,i+4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,j)^{′} \\  & =-16\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\,i-16\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the magnitude of the acceleration as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}||a(t)|| & =\sqrt{(-16\operatorname{cos}⁡4t)^{2}+(-16\operatorname{sin}⁡4t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{16}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡4t+{16}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡4t} \\  & =\sqrt{{16}^{2}} \\  & =16\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the magnitude of the acceleration is $16\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.$

Note that $||a||$ is constant, but $a$ is not. 

**Method 2**

For uniform circular motion in the $xy$-plane, we have

$$
a=-{\omega }^{2}r\,⇒\,||a||={\omega }^{2}||r||.
$$

In our case, the radius of the circle is $a=1\,\text{m}$ and the angular frequency $\omega =4\,\text{rad/s}.$ Therefore,

$$
||a||={4}^{2}\cdot 1=16\,{\text{m/s}}^{2}.
$$

canonical_examples.problem: An object moves along a circular path with position $\mathbf {r}(t)= 5\cos \pi t \, \mathbf i + 5\sin \pi t \,\mathbf j$ meters. Find the speed of the object at time $t,$ measured in seconds.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

First, we find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(r(t))^{′} \\  & =(5\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi t\,i+5\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi t\,j)^{′} \\  & =-5\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi t\,i+5\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the speed, we calculate the magnitude of the velocity vector as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}||v(t)|| & =\sqrt{(-5\pi \operatorname{sin}⁡\pi t)^{2}+(5\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{25{\pi }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\pi t+25{\pi }^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\pi t} \\  & =\sqrt{25{\pi }^{2}({sin}^{2}⁡\pi t+{cos}^{2}⁡\pi t)} \\  & =5\pi \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the object's speed is $5 \pi \textrm{ m/s}.$

Note that the speed is constant, but the velocity is not. 

**Method 2**

For uniform circular motion in the $xy$-plane, we have

$$
||\mathbf v|| = R|\omega|,
$$

where $R$ is the radius of the circle, and $\omega$ is the angular velocity.

In our case, the radius of the circle is $R=5\,\textrm m$ and the angular frequency $\omega = \pi \,\textrm{rad/s}.$ Therefore,

$$
||\mathbf v|| = 5\cdot |\pi| = 5\pi \textrm{ m/s}.
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Acceleration of a Particle Moving With Circular Motion
canonical_examples.problem: An object moves along a circular path with position $\mathbf {r}(t)= 4(\cos 3t\,  \mathbf i + \sin 3t\, \mathbf j)$ meters. Find the magnitude of the acceleration of the object at time $t,$ measured in seconds.
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

First, we find the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =(r(t))^{′} \\  & =(4(\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\,i+\operatorname{sin}⁡3t\,j))^{′} \\  & =-12\operatorname{sin}⁡3t\,i+12\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we find the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector. 

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =(v(t))^{′} \\  & =(-12\operatorname{sin}⁡3t\,i+12\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\,j)^{′} \\  & =-36\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\,i-36\operatorname{sin}⁡3t\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the magnitude of the acceleration as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}||a(t)|| & =\sqrt{(-36\operatorname{cos}⁡3t)^{2}+(-36\operatorname{sin}⁡3t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{36}^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡3t+{36}^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡3t} \\  & =\sqrt{{36}^{2}} \\  & =36\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the magnitude of the acceleration is $36\, \textrm{m/s}^2.$

Note that $||\mathbf a||$ is constant, but $\mathbf a$ is not.

**Method 2**

For uniform circular motion in the $xy$-plane, we have

$$
\mathbf a = -\omega^2\mathbf r \qquad \Rightarrow \qquad ||\mathbf a|| = \omega^2||\mathbf r||.
$$

In our case, the radius of the circle is $R=4\,\textrm m$ and the angular frequency $\omega = 3\,\textrm{rad/s}.$ Therefore,

$$
||\mathbf a|| = 3^2\cdot |4| = 36\, \textrm{m/s}^2.
$$
